reviews.comment: Not worth your time or energy. Save yourself and find another 300 level that will actually challenge you.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Honestly my favorite professor I had this semester. He can be a tough grader and there are a lot of papers you have to write but he gives thorough feedback that is really helpful to improve. Overall he is very nice and very caring and you can tell he is passionate about what he teaches.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Harsh grader but very kind man he gives lots of detailed feedback on each essay which there were like 12 through the semester. Lectures were not that important but they were interesting. Every essay is based on watching a historical film and creating an analysis.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: You will have to read a lot! There is a textbook that I would read. He does not cover stuff from the textbook in lecture. You will have to read three books and write papers on them. The prompts for those papers were not great. The papers are toughly graded. He takes attendance in every class and for a grade although he does allow a few absences.

I took him for 436 (not 101) and it was his first semester teaching it. It was rough to say the least. He was always late and went over time, but the worst thing about him was that he gave absolutely no instructions for assignments and then graded you really hard on them and took off points for not following the instructions (that were not given).

The lectures were a little disorganized but overall it is an easy class to pass. We had to read 3 books and write a paper on each which seemed like a bit much. However, he gives you great feedback and I feel I've come out of the class a much better writer. He doesn't use ppt and just writes outlines on the board which was hard to read at times.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--So many papers

reviews.comment: Not my favorite professor, I would not recommend him. Lectures were very boring and his voice is monotone. He was late to almost every class and went past class time. Our assignments were all essays and he took forever to grade them. Overall was not a great class experience and I do not think I learned a lot from this class
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He was very disorganized. Lectures always ran over. Outlines were given twenty minutes before class started and he rarely covered all of the material. We were supposed to have a textbook but never received it. The exams did not cover information that was covered in lecture. We had to research information that we had never gone over before.

Extensive readings but they are interesting. He isn't the best at feedback when it comes to essays but he is a solid choice for becoming a better writer. Had a B the whole semester but got an A after the last paper. As long as you work for it, you'll pass the class but it is difficult.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Idk why he has some negative reviews because I just took him and hes one of the better professors Ive had. He helped me with my final research paper for the two months leading up to when it was due, so by the time I submitted all the mistakes were gone. he cares about the topic and overall he is just a genuine guy. definitely take him if you can!
I took Dr. Haefeli's religion in early America class and very much enjoyed it. Haefeli does a really good job of helping you grow as a critical thinker and writing. Would highly recommend :)
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: His tests are reading heavy and involve critical thinking, but for a history class, I wouldn't really expect anything else. The class is entirely test-based for the majority of your grade, but the weight of the tests go up with the amount of time in class. If you read, participate in class, and take good notes you're good. Take your time with exams
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I've taken him for two classes and made A's in both.  If you show up, pay attention, and aren't an idiot, you'll should do fairly well.  Most of the grade is determined by a handful of papers.  Don't ever use the passive in your papers.  Fair warning, if you aren't particularly skilled at writing, I wouldn't recommend taking him for anything.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: He knows what he's talking about and he makes you read so that you can be able to discuss the topics with him. I had to rent EIGHT textbooks! I didn't do all the reading but I had to at least skim every assigned passage. 25% of your grade is participating in discussions! All tests are take home prompted papers. He's a tough grader but I got an A!!!
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Worst professor I have EVER had. The lectures have absolutely nothing to do with the graded assignments (papers). Incredibly slow & hard grader. He has no idea what he's looking for when he grades/how to grade. I'm a very strong writer & the best grade I made was a B- with the help of the UWC & 2 weeks of work. His page limits make them impossible.

This course broke my 4.0. Graded on 5 essays that are on topics completely different from lectures, which are not ever tested for comprehension. Said that since he taught at Ivy League schools, "I don't see why you should be graded on a lesser standard." Out of 50 students, gave 1 A and 2 B's on the first essay. The same pattern then on.
He requires attendance, His tests are not based on lecture AT ALL! Be prepared to write like you're a student at an Ivy League.
